newsitem.title: USA: Frontier Airlines hopes to expand fleet.
newsitem.headline: Frontier Airlines hopes to expand fleet.

text.p: Frontier Airlines Inc Chief Executive Officer Sam Addoms said on Friday the company hoped to lease three more airplanes by the end of March 1997.
The Denver-based airline currently has a fleet of nine aircraft and has signed a lease for a 10th to be delivered in April 1997.
All told, it wants to add five more by 1998, bringing its total to 18 aircraft, he said.
Addoms said the airline-leasing market was "tight" partly because carriers are holding on to their fleets longer rather than buying newer planes.
He also said that Frontier, which specializes in low fares, was passing along to customers only about half of the 10 percent federal excise tax.
He said it was difficult to tell when Frontier would pass on the full 10 percent tax, if ever. "We aren't the price maker. We reflect what other people are doing," he said.

Addoms said Frontier may be able to "approach in a year" its goal of lowering its operating costs to 7.5 cents per avaiable seat mile from the current 8.6 cents, assuming a fleet of 14 to 15 airplanes.
Addoms made his remarks at the company's annual meeting in Denver.
